```{r setup, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  dpi = 600,
  dev.args = list(bg = NA)
)

library(ggplot2)
library(eulerr)

f_col <- "#E86F77"
h_col <- "#4192D9"
fh_col <- "#9075AB"
identity_col <- adjustcolor("#A6A6A6", alpha.f = 0.85)

read_pileup <- function(path) {
  x <- read.table(path, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (ncol(x) < 5) {
    stop("Expected at least five columns in ", path)
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(x$V5)) {
    stop("Peak identifiers are not unique in ", path)
  }
  data.frame(pileup = x$V4, row.names = x$V5)
}

mean_replicates <- function(rep1, rep2) {
  common <- intersect(row.names(rep1), row.names(rep2))
  data.frame(
    pileup = (rep1[common, "pileup"] + rep2[common, "pileup"]) / 2,
    row.names = common
  )
}

prepare_comparison <- function(single_line, dual_line, overlap_peaks) {
  common <- intersect(row.names(single_line), row.names(dual_line))
  overlap_peaks <- intersect(common, overlap_peaks)

  # Reproduce 240103_k1f_modeling.R exactly: fit log(y) = log(x) + b
  # across all positive finite peaks, then divide x by exp(-b).
  x <- single_line[common, "pileup"]
  y <- dual_line[common, "pileup"]
  norm_keep <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y) & x > 0 & y > 0
  norm_fit <- lm(log(y[norm_keep]) ~ offset(log(x[norm_keep])))
  norm_factor <- 1 / exp(unname(coef(norm_fit)[[1]]))

  out <- data.frame(
    peak = common,
    single = x / norm_factor,
    dual = y,
    overlap = common %in% overlap_peaks,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # Match test_diff() in 240103_k1f_modeling.R: exclude non-positive values
  # and calculate the ratio without a pseudocount.
  ratio_keep <- is.finite(out$single) & is.finite(out$dual) &
    out$single > 0 & out$dual > 0
  out$log2_fc <- NA_real_
  out$log2_fc[ratio_keep] <- log2(
    out$dual[ratio_keep] / out$single[ratio_keep]
  )

  test_values <- out$log2_fc[out$overlap & is.finite(out$log2_fc)]
  if (length(test_values) == 0) {
    stop("No finite overlap-peak fold changes were available for testing")
  }

  # Fit log2(y) = log2(x) + b to the positive overlap peaks. Fixing the
  # log-scale slope at one makes 2^b the geometric-mean fold difference and
  # gives each peak equal influence in proportional rather than absolute units.
  fit_keep <- out$overlap & is.finite(out$single) & is.finite(out$dual) &
    out$single > 0 & out$dual > 0
  fold_fit <- lm(
    log2(dual) ~ offset(log2(single)),
    data = out[fit_keep, , drop = FALSE]
  )
  log2_fold <- unname(coef(fold_fit)[["(Intercept)"]])
  fold_change <- 2^log2_fold
  fold_change_confint <- 2^unname(
    confint(fold_fit, "(Intercept)", level = 0.95)
  )

  test <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(
    test_values,
    mu = 0,
    alternative = "greater",
    exact = FALSE,
    conf.int = TRUE
  ))

  list(
    data = out,
    norm_factor = norm_factor,
    norm_fit = norm_fit,
    test = test,
    fold_fit = fold_fit,
    log2_fold = log2_fold,
    fold_change = fold_change,
    fold_change_confint = fold_change_confint,
    n_fit = sum(fit_keep),
    n_overlap = length(test_values),
    median_fold = 2^median(test_values, na.rm = TRUE),
    wilcox_fold = if (length(test$estimate)) 2^unname(test$estimate) else NA_real_,
    fold_confint = if (!is.null(test$conf.int)) 2^test$conf.int else c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
  )
}

format_p <- function(p) {
  if (!is.finite(p)) return("NA")
  if (p < 2.2e-16) return("<2.2e-16")
  format.pval(p, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4)
}

sparse_log_ticks <- function(lim, max_ticks = 4) {
  tick_exp <- seq(
    ceiling(log10(lim[1])),
    floor(log10(lim[2]))
  )

  if (length(tick_exp) > max_ticks) {
    keep <- unique(round(seq(1, length(tick_exp), length.out = max_ticks)))
    tick_exp <- tick_exp[keep]
  }

  if (length(tick_exp) == 0) {
    tick_at <- pretty(lim, n = max_ticks)
    tick_at <- tick_at[tick_at > 0 & tick_at >= lim[1] & tick_at <= lim[2]]
    return(list(at = tick_at, labels = format(tick_at, trim = TRUE)))
  }

  list(
    at = 10^tick_exp,
    labels = parse(text = paste0("10^", tick_exp))
  )
}

plot_binding_comparison <- function(result, xlab, ylab, title,
                                    base_col, overlap_col = fh_col) {
  dat <- result$data
  keep <- is.finite(dat$single) & is.finite(dat$dual) &
    dat$single > 0 & dat$dual > 0
  dat <- dat[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  lim <- range(c(dat$single, dat$dual), finite = TRUE)
  log_lim <- log10(lim)
  pad <- diff(log_lim) * 0.04
  if (!is.finite(pad) || pad == 0) pad <- 0.1
  lim <- 10^(log_lim + c(-pad, pad))

  old_par <- par(
    mar = c(3.8, 3.8, 2.5, 0.7),
    mgp = c(1.75, 0.35, 0),
    tcl = -0.22,
    las = 1,
    cex.axis = 0.78,
    cex.lab = 0.85
  )
  on.exit(par(old_par), add = TRUE)

  plot(
    dat$single, dat$dual,
    log = "xy",
    xlim = lim, ylim = lim,
    pch = 16, cex = 0.75,
    col = adjustcolor(base_col, alpha.f = 0.28),
    axes = FALSE,
    ann = FALSE,
    asp = 1
  )
  lines(lim, lim, col = identity_col, lwd = 1.2, lty = 5)
  fit_x <- range(dat$single[dat$overlap], finite = TRUE)
  points(
    dat$single[dat$overlap], dat$dual[dat$overlap],
    pch = 16, cex = 0.75,
    col = "white"
  )
  points(
    dat$single[dat$overlap], dat$dual[dat$overlap],
    pch = 16, cex = 0.75,
    col = adjustcolor(overlap_col, alpha.f = 0.5)
  )
  lines(
    fit_x, result$fold_change * fit_x,
    col = adjustcolor(overlap_col, alpha.f = 0.9),
    lwd = 1.3
  )
  major_ticks <- sparse_log_ticks(lim, max_ticks = 4)
  axis(1, at = major_ticks$at, labels = major_ticks$labels,
       lwd = 0, lwd.ticks = 0.7)
  axis(2, at = major_ticks$at, labels = major_ticks$labels,
       lwd = 0, lwd.ticks = 0.7)
  box(lwd = 0.8)
  title(xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, line = 1.75, cex.lab = 0.85)
  title(main = title, line = 0.65, cex.main = 0.9, font.main = 1)

  lx <- log10(lim)
  label_x <- 10^(lx[1] + 0.04 * diff(lx))
  label_y <- 10^(lx[2] - 0.04 * diff(lx))
  label <- sprintf("y = %.2fx", result$fold_change)
  text(label_x, label_y, labels = label, adj = c(0, 1), cex = 0.67)
}

```

## Single-factor versus F-H-inducible cell lines

Highlighted points are peaks in the FOXA1--HNF4A overlap lists. The dashed line
is the identity line. The colored line is obtained by fitting
$\log_2(y)=\log_2(x)+b$ to the positive highlighted peaks, and $2^b$ is reported
as the fold difference. Single-factor signals are scaled to the total signal
in the corresponding F-H-inducible dataset before plotting.

```{r binding-scatter, fig.width=6., fig.height=3.15, fig.align='center'}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot_binding_comparison(
  foxa1_result,
  xlab = "iFOXA1",
  ylab = "iFH",
  title = "FOXA1 binding signal [a.u.]",
  base_col = f_col,
  overlap_col = fh_col
)

plot_binding_comparison(
  hnf4a_result,
  xlab = "iHNF4A",
  ylab = "iFH",
  title = "HNF4A binding signal [a.u.]",
  base_col = h_col,
  overlap_col = fh_col
)
```

```{r peak-color-legend, fig.width=5.4, fig.height=0.65, fig.align='center'}
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot.new()
legend(
  "center",
  legend = c("FOXA1 peak", "HNF4A peak", "Overlapping FH peak"),
  pch = 16,
  col = c(f_col, h_col, fh_col),
  pt.cex = 0.9,
  cex = 0.78,
  bty = "n",
  horiz = TRUE,
  xpd = NA
)
```

## FOXA1 and HNF4A peak overlap

The Euler diagram follows the style used in Figure 1. Circle areas and labels
show peak-set sizes, with translucent FOXA1 and HNF4A fills producing a
purple-shaded overlap. If the two reciprocal overlap lists differ in length,
the smaller count is used as a conservative shared intersection.

```{r peak-overlap-venn, fig.width=3, fig.height=2.2, fig.align='center'}
foxa1_peak_set <- unique(row.names(foxa1_k1f_0d5_mean))
hnf4a_peak_set <- unique(row.names(hnf4a_k3h_0d5_mean))
foxa1_overlap_set <- intersect(foxa1_peak_set, unique(fh_overlap_foxa1))
hnf4a_overlap_set <- intersect(hnf4a_peak_set, unique(fh_overlap_hnf4a))

n_f_overlap <- length(foxa1_overlap_set)
n_h_overlap <- length(hnf4a_overlap_set)
overlap_n <- min(n_f_overlap, n_h_overlap)

if (n_f_overlap != n_h_overlap) {
  warning(
    "Reciprocal overlap counts differ (FOXA1 = ", n_f_overlap,
    ", HNF4A = ", n_h_overlap,
    "); using the smaller count in the Euler diagram."
  )
}

peak_overlap_counts <- c(
  "FOXA1" = length(foxa1_peak_set) - overlap_n,
  "HNF4A" = length(hnf4a_peak_set) - overlap_n,
  "FOXA1&HNF4A" = overlap_n
)

peak_overlap_fit <- euler(peak_overlap_counts)
plot(
  peak_overlap_fit,
  labels = list(
    labels = c("FOXA1 peak", "HNF4A peak"),
    font = 1,
    cex = 0.9
  ),
  quantities = list(
    labels = c(
      as.character(peak_overlap_counts[["FOXA1"]]),
      as.character(peak_overlap_counts[["HNF4A"]]),
      paste0("Overlapping\npeak\n", peak_overlap_counts[["FOXA1&HNF4A"]])
    ),
    font = 1,
    cex = 0.9
  ),
  fills = list(fill = c(f_col, h_col), alpha = 0.38),
  edges = list(col = c(f_col, h_col), lwd = 4)
)
```

## Fold-change distributions at overlap peaks

The one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test is performed on per-peak
$\log_2(\mathrm{F\mbox{-}H}/\mathrm{single\ factor})$ values. Testing on the
log scale makes the comparison proportional rather than dependent on absolute
signal differences across the wide CUT&Tag dynamic range.

```{r overlap-fold-change, fig.width=3.2, fig.height=3.1, fig.align='center'}
fc_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    factor = "FOXA1",
    log2_fc = foxa1_result$data$log2_fc[foxa1_result$data$overlap]
  ),
  data.frame(
    factor = "HNF4A",
    log2_fc = hnf4a_result$data$log2_fc[hnf4a_result$data$overlap]
  )
)
fc_df <- fc_df[is.finite(fc_df$log2_fc), , drop = FALSE]
fc_df$factor <- factor(fc_df$factor, levels = c("FOXA1", "HNF4A"))

set.seed(1)
boxplot(
  log2_fc ~ factor,
  data = fc_df,
  col = c(adjustcolor(f_col, alpha.f = 0.35),
          adjustcolor(h_col, alpha.f = 0.35)),
  border = c(f_col, h_col),
  outline = FALSE,
  boxwex = 0.42,
  staplewex = 0,
  axes = FALSE,
  ann = FALSE
)
stripchart(
  log2_fc ~ factor,
  data = fc_df,
  vertical = TRUE,
  method = "jitter",
  jitter = 0.14,
  add = TRUE,
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.38,
  col = c(adjustcolor(f_col, alpha.f = 0.5),
          adjustcolor(h_col, alpha.f = 0.5))
)
abline(h = 0, lty = 5, lwd = 1, col = identity_col)
axis(1, at = 1:2, labels = c("FOXA1", "HNF4A"),
     lwd = 0, lwd.ticks = 0.7, cex.axis = 0.8)
axis(2, lwd = 0, lwd.ticks = 0.7, las = 1, cex.axis = 0.8)
box(lwd = 0.8)
title(
  ylab = expression(log[2]("F-H line"/"single-factor line")),
  line = 2.2,
  cex.lab = 0.85
)
```

## Statistical summary

```{r statistical-summary, results='asis'}
summary_table <- data.frame(
  Factor = c("FOXA1", "HNF4A"),
  `Positive overlap peaks in fit (n)` = c(foxa1_result$n_fit,
                                           hnf4a_result$n_fit),
  `Log-scale regression fold (2^b)` = round(
    c(foxa1_result$fold_change, hnf4a_result$fold_change),
    2
  ),
  `Fold 95% CI` = c(
    sprintf("%.2f--%.2f", foxa1_result$fold_change_confint[1],
            foxa1_result$fold_change_confint[2]),
    sprintf("%.2f--%.2f", hnf4a_result$fold_change_confint[1],
            hnf4a_result$fold_change_confint[2])
  ),
  `One-sided paired Wilcoxon P` = c(
    format_p(foxa1_result$test$p.value),
    format_p(hnf4a_result$test$p.value)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(summary_table, booktabs = TRUE, align = "lrrrr")
```
